title: One detail in stone. Two places learning together.
lead: A visitor pauses at a carved wheel. What helps them see more than a beautiful photograph? That question could begin a conversation between two coastal heritage places.
context: We are exploring a possible learning exchange between Konark in Odisha and Mamallapuram in Tamil Nadu. No counterpart, participant or activity has been agreed.

places.name: Konark
places.text: The thirteenth-century Sun Temple gives architectural form to Surya’s chariot, within the Kalingan tradition.

places.name: Mamallapuram
places.text: Pallava monuments from the seventh and eighth centuries bring together rock-cut sanctuaries, monolithic rathas, reliefs and structural temples.

difference: Different periods. Different traditions. A shared question about helping people understand what they see. This comparison does not establish an ancient connection or a modern town partnership.

outputs.title: Two stories to carry home
outputs.text: Willing local contributors could each explain one detail, with a permitted image, sources and a question for a future visit.

outputs.title: A conversation in both directions
outputs.text: A small remote session could help participants compare explanations and correct what an unfamiliar reader might misunderstand.

outputs.title: Something useful for each place
outputs.text: Each side would receive credited material it can reuse. Local interest, language review, permissions, time and costs would shape any next step.
